correctness.rationale: On the blow-up of six general points, the 27 line classes have plane degrees 0,1,2. Three distinct classes summing to −K have degree patterns (0,1,2) and (1,1,1). The exceptional coefficients in the two cases force, respectively, E_i+L_ij+Q_j for ordered i≠j, and three L_ab for a partition of the six indices into pairs. Each such effective anticanonical sum is the section by a plane. This gives the 45 tritangent triples, independent of the chosen smooth complex surface, including the possibility of concurrency of the lines in a triple. I built the incidence directly from the ordered indices and perfect matchings. On deleting a curve vertex and a plane vertex, independent FLINT integer Smith and determinant computations both gave 1^42,3^10,9^5,27^8,135^6 and 3^62·5^6. The determinant is nonzero, so the graph is connected; 135 edges and 72 vertices give cycle rank 64, and the exponent is 135. This is ordinary graph torsion, not torsion of a divisor group of the surface itself.
residual_risks: Uses the classical smooth-complex cubic-surface class lists; no positive-characteristic, geometric Picard or descent claim is being verified.

evidence: Theorem 5 covers the even-unitary Hermitian point graphs of dimension at least four. At q=2,m=2,ℓ=3, the field is F4 and this is the cross-characteristic case ℓ | q+1, ℓ ∤ m and ℓ ∤ m−1.

Using the proof in §12.2.0.2, subcase 1(2), its variables are f=20, g=24, c=v3(q^(2m−1)+1)=2 and d=v3(q^(2m−3)+1)=1. The dimension relations in §§7 and 12.1 give dim V^r=f, dim(V^r/U)=(q^(2m)−1)/(q+1)=5, dim(U/U′)=1, so x=dim U′=14. The proof gives e_c=f−x−1=5, e_d=g−x=10, e_(c+d)=x=14, and e_0=x+1=15 on the 45-vertex full Laplacian, with one zero factor. The proof's variable assignments and dimension identities fix the interpretation rather than relying on the extracted summary table alone.
broader_coverage.reasoning: This supplies exactly the full 3-primary critical group of the dual point graph needed after Schur reduction, not merely a p-rank. Its valuation sum 10+2·5+3·14=62 agrees with the independent determinant.

evidence: Over Z_(3), eliminate 5I_27; up to the unit 1/5 the remaining matrix is 15I_45−N^TN. Its diagonal is 12 and off-diagonals are minus adjacency precisely when planes share a line. Thus it is the ordinary Laplacian of H(3,4)'s point graph and has 3-primary factors 3^10,9^5,27^14 in multiplicity notation.

Over Z_(5) eliminate 3I_45 instead. The residual matrix up to a unit is 15I_27−NN^T=10I−A. The sum-zero lattice splits because 27 is a 5-unit. On it the eigenvalues 9 and 15 have respective multiplicities 20 and 6 and unit difference modulo 5, so the integral polynomial projectors give (Z/5)^6. No other primes occur by the tree determinant; pairing the last six order-27 factors with these six order-5 factors gives the original 135^6.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: All the frozen Smith factors follow from an earlier general theorem and routine prime-local block elimination; no separate hard Smith calculation, additional geometric hypothesis or priority inference is required.

evidence: The graph is the Levi graph of GQ(2,4), unchanged when written as the dual order-(4,2) Hermitian quadrangle H(3,4) with incidence parts exchanged. The 45-vertex point graph of this dual quadrangle is Γ_ue(2,2), the isotropic one-spaces in a four-dimensional Hermitian space over F4 joined by orthogonality.

The 27-vertex collinearity graph has parameters (27,10,1,5), while the dual collinearity graph has (45,12,3,3). Neither point graph is the same as the Levi graph; the precise prime-local reduction connects them.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The dual alias is isomorphic as an uncoloured incidence graph. The point-graph identities give a reduction, not a claim that any graph with the same SRG parameters has the same Smith form. As a bipartite graph with unequal degrees 5 and 3 it is not ordinary distance-regular.
